title: Polynomial-Time Encoding of a Gate Fragment
statement: Let $\ell$ be a natural number, let $p$ be a Boolean function on bit strings of length $\ell$, and let $w(z,j)$ assign a natural number to each bit string $z$ and natural number $j$. Suppose that for every $j<\ell$, the function sending $z$ to the unary string of $w(z,j)$ ones is polynomial-time computable. Then the function that sends $z$ to the binary fragment encoding of the CNF gate obtained by relabeling the truth-table clauses for $p$ using the wire indices $w(z,j)$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean function on bit strings of length $\ell$.
A wire-index function $w$ from bit strings and natural numbers to natural numbers.
For every $j<\ell$, the unary encoding of $w(z,j)$ is polynomial-time computable.
